agent_fix.defect: awaited two synchronous matchers and passed domain_id where the keyword is domain; both TypeErrors were swallowed by contextlib.suppress, so terms and rules were always empty
agent_fix.change: call GlossaryManager.match / RuleEngine.match synchronously with domain=; replace suppress with explicit capture into metadata term_match_error / rule_match_error
agent_fix.before_fix: 5 failed, 10 passed (verified by stashing the source change and rerunning the same file)
agent_fix.downstream: terms/rules are only forwarded into orchestrator/collaboration output; prompt building uses a character budget of the same name, so the prompt text does not change

findings.class: lock-path handling on local filesystems: symlinks, ignored mode, marker files, SQLite-backed read/write locks

blocker.reason: litellm requires filelock>=3.16.1,<4.0 and the latest published litellm (1.106.6) still does so
blocker.verified: PyPI metadata for litellm 1.106.6: requires_dist contains 'filelock<4.0,>=3.16.1'
blocker.consequence: the fix cannot be installed without dropping or downgrading litellm; no 3.x backport of the fixes exists
blocker.exposure: the project never imports filelock directly; it is reached only through litellm (and a >=3.10 constraint from huggingface_hub). Preconditions in the advisories are a local attacker able to plant files or symlinks in the lock directory, which the single-host private deployment does not provide by default

verification.rollback: reinstalled 30.18.0; tests/test_core went from 383 passed + 330 failed back to 713 passed

sqlglot.decision: keep 30.18.0; adapting to the new qualify() signature is a code change with its own verification, not a version bump
